# Pre-registration G: family-wise test over ranks 2-4, sibling-model test, one validity rule
Written 2026-10-13, BEFORE any run of G. Do not change after results exist; record deviations in a
"Deviations" section of the output, with the reason.

Motivation: hostile round 2 (scratchpad/attack2_hostile.md item 1). The paper's per-rank 1% + contiguous-
from-rank-2 rule finds nothing beyond ability on all-4; ranks 3-4 sit at the 97-99th pct of the valid 2PL and
Rasch nulls, and a post-hoc joint statistic rejects. We fix the statistic here, before looking.

## G1. Family-wise statistic (primary)
- T = max over r in {2,3,4} of pct_r, where pct_r = fraction of null draws with lambda_r(null) < lambda_r(obs)
  (ties count half). Null distribution of T: for each null draw d, compute its own max_r pct_r against the
  other draws (leave-one-out). p_T = (1 + #{d: T_d >= T_obs}) / (1 + n_draws).
- Secondary (report, no decision): S = lambda2+lambda3+lambda4, p_S same way.
- Draws: 2000 NEW null draws per (score, null), seeds disjoint from all earlier runs (new seed namespace "G").
- Applied to: rotation 0 and all six rotation scorings (>=1, >=2, >=3, all-4, mean ... whatever the construction
  family in v3_softpref.py step1 has), under every null that is VALID by the single rule below.
- Decision level: alpha = 0.05 family-wise (chosen to be strict AGAINST our current "nothing beyond ability" claim).

## G2. Calibration of the G1 test under soft-preference (SP) truth
- Datasets simulated from the SP fit (common tau, no second factor), conditioned on the observed unparsed mask,
  exactly as in step2b. 200 datasets per score for rotation 0 and all-4 (others if budget allows).
- For each: refit the 2PL and Rasch on the simulated data, draw 500 null draws each, compute p_T.
- Report the false-positive rate FP = P(p_T < 0.05). If FP > 0.10, the G1 decision uses the calibrated threshold
  (the 5th percentile of p_T under SP truth) and both raw and calibrated p are reported.

## G3. Power of the G1 test
- Same planted subject-block factor as the existing power study (STEM block, s in {1, 2}), 200 datasets each,
  all-4 score, 2PL and Rasch nulls. Report detection rate of G1 at alpha 0.05 (raw and calibrated).

## G4. Sibling-model test (lineage)
- Sibling rule, fixed from model metadata, NOT from correlations: two models are siblings if they are fine-tunes
  or successive versions of the same base model at the same parameter count. Clusters:
  {Phi-3-mini-4k, Phi-3.5-mini}, {Meta-Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B}, {Mistral-7B-v0.2, Mistral-7B-v0.3, zephyr-7b-beta},
  {Qwen2-7B, Qwen2.5-7B}. (Ministral-8B, Mistral-Small, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Gemma-2-2b/9b, Qwen2.5 0.5/1.5/3B differ
  in size -> not siblings.)
- Run G1 (2PL and Rasch, all-4; also rotation 0) on EVERY subset that keeps exactly one model per cluster
  (2*2*3*2 = 24 subsets, 24-5 = 19 models each), refitting the nulls per subset; 1000 draws per subset.
- Report the distribution of p_T and of ranks-beyond-ability across the 24 subsets.
- Control: the same number (5) of models removed at random from non-sibling models, 24 random subsets, same seed rule.

## G5. Single validity rule everywhere
- Rule (Sec. 2): a null is valid iff observed lambda1 lies within its 1st-99th pct. No second "calibrated validity".
- Recompute Table A2's SP column by this rule (all-4 SP: invalid; rotation 0 SP: valid -> report its rank-2 p).
- Recompute the power study's SP-rule column so that it applies the procedure the paper uses on real data.

## G6. Unparsed-reply variants (hostile minor 7)
- Rerun the valid nulls (rotation 0: letter-aware rot-0 fit and 3PL; all-4: 2PL and Rasch) with per-rank AND G1
  on the drop and impute variants of the unparsed replies. 1000 draws.

## Decision rules for the claim (fixed now)
A. G1 on all-4 does not reject (calibrated) under 2PL or Rasch -> current claim stands, with G3 power caveat.
B. G1 rejects under both valid nulls, and in >= 18 of 24 sibling subsets it no longer rejects (while the random-
   removal control keeps rejecting in most) -> claim: "no second direction separates at rank 2; a weaker excess at
   ranks 3-4 follows model lineage (sibling models)". Letter preference = the largest structure beyond ability,
   not the only one.
C. G1 rejects and sibling removal does not remove it -> claim: "structure beyond ability remains at ranks 3-4,
   of unknown source"; the paper must say so in the abstract.
Mixed outcomes are reported as they are, with the nearest rule named.
meta.statistic:
G. Pre-registered family-wise test over ranks 2-4, sibling-model test, one validity rule
(pre-registration: scratchpad prereg_G.md, written 2026-10-13 before any G run; quoted in the output).

Parts (python v3_G_familywise.py <part>):
  run      : G1, G2, G3, G4, G6 in one pool (checkpointed per job under results/analysis/logs_G/ckpt).
  assemble : G5 (from stored F outputs) and the summary results/analysis/v3_G_familywise.json + raw files.
  all      : run, then assemble.

Statistic (G1). Null eigenvalue sample E (n draws, ranks 1..4), observed obs.
  pct_r(obs)   = 100 (#{d: E_dr < obs_r} + #{d: E_dr = obs_r} / 2) / n       (= v3_softpref.pct_of)
  T            = max_{r in 2,3,4} pct_r(obs)
  T_d          = max_{r in 2,3,4} pct_r(E_d) against the other n - 1 draws (leave-one-out)
  p_T          = (1 + #{d: T_d >= T}) / (1 + n)
  S            = lambda_2 + lambda_3 + lambda_4,  p_S = (1 + #{d: S_d >= S}) / (1 + n)   (secondary, no decision)
All percentiles are kept as integer half-counts h = 2 #{<} + #{=} (pct = 100 h / (2 n)), and T_d >= T is
tested exactly by integer cross-multiplication: T_d >= T <=> h_d n >= h_obs (n - 1).
Validity (G5, one rule everywhere): p01 <= observed lambda_1 <= p99 of the null lambda_1
(v3_softpref.lambda1_valid). G1 rejects a (score, null) iff the null is valid and p_T < 0.05 (raw), or,
where the G2 false-positive rate exceeds 0.10, p_T < the 5th percentile of p_T under SP truth (calibrated).

Every null, fit and simulation is the existing code: v3_across.run_suite / run_null / Context / kg_fits,
v3_softpref.simulate_choices / sp_null / load_base / variant_data / SCORES / family_nulls /
lambda1_valid / rank_summary, v2lib.impute_column_mean. Seeds: new namespace SEED_G (see rng_g).

G5_single_validity_rule.rule: a null is valid iff p01 <= observed lambda_1 <= p99 of its lambda_1 (lambda1_valid); no calibrated validity

decision.why: G1 rejects under both nulls; >= 18 of 24 sibling subsets no longer reject; the control mostly rejects

Deviations: G1 null set: 'every null that is VALID' is read as the step-1 suite of each score (v3_softpref.family_nulls) plus the primary soft-preference null (common tau, base fit). The tau = 0, per-model tau, penalty and bootstrap-averaged SP variants are sensitivity fits and are not included. Validity is decided on the 2000 NEW draws of each null, so it can differ from step 1 near the 1st/99th percentile.
G1 data: the full 24-model data only (the pre-registration names no data variants; the no-Llama-3.2-1B and no-option-referencing variants are not rerun).
G1 'against the other draws' is implemented literally: T_d uses the other n - 1 NULL draws (the observed value is not among them), T_obs uses all n draws.

G2 calibrates the G1 test only for the 2PL and Rasch (as pre-registered). Rotation 0 and all-4 are the pre-registered scores; >=1, >=2, >=3 were added because the budget allowed (the mean score has no 2PL/Rasch). G2 p_T uses 500 null draws, the real-data G1 p_T uses 2000: the calibrated threshold (5th percentile of the 500-draw p_T) is applied to the 2000-draw p_T (both estimate the same p; the 500-draw grid is 1/501).

Found after the run (caveat, not a change): where T saturates at 100 (rotation 0, >=1, >=2, >=3 under most nulls), p_T is set by the number of null draws whose own LOO T also reaches 100, so it sits at a few grid steps (2000 draws: about 0.002; 500 draws: 0.006-0.008). There, comparing a 2000-draw p_T with a 500-draw calibrated threshold is a grid artifact: the calibrated G1 decisions for >=2 (2PL reject) and >=3 (2PL, Rasch no reject) are not reliable. The all-4 decisions do not saturate (T = 98.6, 99.1) and use the raw threshold (G2 FP = 0).
G2 datasets use new seeds (namespace G), not the step-2b datasets; the step-2b pipeline is reproduced exactly on 2 of its own datasets in the tests.

G3 uses 500 null draws per dataset (the pre-registration gives no number; equal to G2 so the calibrated threshold applies). s = 0 is not rerun: its size is G2's all-4 false-positive rate (same pipeline).

G4 rotation 0: the 2PL and Rasch are run as named, plus the nulls valid on the full rotation-0 data (3PL, KG uniform, letter-aware), since G1 applies to valid nulls only; validity is decided per subset. A subset 'rejects' on all-4 when G1 rejects under at least one of the two nulls (both counts reported). The G2 threshold (24 models) is reported for the 19-model subsets as a reference only; the subset decisions use the raw alpha = 0.05.

G5 power column: 'the procedure the paper uses on real data' after G5 = plain validity AND rank-2 percentile above the calibrated 99% threshold; computed from the stored power datasets (no new simulation).

G6 drop on all-4: two definitions are run, drop_affected (questions with an all-4 entry decided by unparsed replies: no parsed rotation wrong and >= 1 unparsed; 95 questions) and drop_any (any unparsed reply in any rotation; 217 questions). Rotation 0 drops the 112 questions with an unparsed rotation-0 reply (as App. B).

G6 impute: the binary nulls cannot be fitted to fractional data, so each null is fitted to the as-scored binary matrix, and the observed matrix and every null draw are imputed at the same cells by v2lib.impute_column_mean (column mean of the other entries); columns constant after imputation are dropped (counts reported). All-4 imputes the entries decided by unparsed replies (124 cells).
